As of the most recent available evidence, Microsoft's acquisition of Activision Blizzard is the largest tech industry buyout in history at $68.7 billion [d8]. This deal, which overcame significant antitrust hurdles in both the U.S. and abroad, surpassed the previous record held by Dell's acquisition of enterprise storage company EMC for approximately $67 billion, announced in 2015 and completed in 2016 [d8][d1][d2]. Earlier sources from 2015 and shortly after identified the Dell-EMC deal as the all-time record for tech acquisitions [d9][d2], but this has since been superseded [d8]. The Microsoft-Activision deal also brought major gaming franchises such as Call of Duty, World of Warcraft, and Candy Crush under Microsoft's umbrella [d8].
